historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported FCF CAGR is not meaningful (not-meaningful/negative in both windows: FY2023 JPY17.0bn -> FY2026 JPY3.4bn, a trough-to-trough collapse driven by capex ramp and margin compression, not a repeatable growth trend). EPS 5yr CAGR is negative (-17.0%, FY2021 JPY152.89 -> FY2026 JPY60.37) reflecting the same margin trough. Equity CAGR (2.3% 5yr, 1.2% 3yr) is the most conservative anchor and is used for growth_rate_source per the method's default hierarchy, but it materially understates what the base-case revenue path assumes (revenue itself grew at a healthier 5.0% 5yr CAGR before the FY2026 dip). The forward revenue path is NOT simply this selected_growth_rate extrapolated -- it is anchored instead to FY2027 guidance (revenue JPY440.0bn, -0.5% YoY) for year 1 and a component-built margin recovery thereafter, per section 2 of owner-fcf.md. The equity CAGR is reported here for the required disclosure but is deliberately not the growth driver of the projection.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-anchored, partial-recovery case: FY2027 revenue follows management's own guidance, then grows modestly on non-Honda diversification while Honda volumes stay roughly flat-to-down; operating margin recovers to ~4.0-4.5% by the end of the horizon, about halfway between the FY2026 trough (2.3%) and management's own 5.0%-by-FY2029 target, discounting the target for the 15th Medium-Term Plan's much larger miss.
scenario_narratives.bull: 16th Medium-Term Plan succeeds: Honda-share gains, non-Honda scale-up toward the JPY100bn FY2029 target, and a stabilizing China franchise let operating margin approach management's stated 5.0% target by year 5, aided by a structurally weaker yen.
scenario_narratives.bear: 16th Medium-Term Plan repeats the 15th's failure: continuing Honda China share loss, a Japan/Americas volume drag, and non-Honda wins too small to offset the core decline hold operating margin near the FY2026 trough through the horizon, with elevated capex not translating into volume.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TS TECH is a structurally sound but currently impaired keiretsu supplier: a genuine, multi-decade Honda-incumbency moat and a large net-cash balance sheet (JPY92.6bn cash, zero interest-bearing debt, against a market cap of roughly JPY204bn at the current price) sit underneath an operating business whose margin has more than halved in two years (9.9% FY2018 peak operating margin to 2.3% FY2026) on Honda volume declines and a rapidly worsening China share loss to domestic EV makers. The valuation is built as a genuine mid-cycle recovery case, not a trough extrapolation and not a full credit-management's-plan case: base-case margins recover to roughly half the distance between the FY2026 trough and management's own 5.0%-by-FY2029 target, because the immediately prior medium-term plan missed an equivalent target by 7 points on the same dynamics that are still worsening today. The terminal cap multiple (12x) and terminal growth (1.5%) are held conservative for a capital-intensive, single-digit-margin, single-customer-dependent auto-parts supplier that has traded below 1x book for most of the last decade (PBR ~0.6x at the current price against JPY311.6bn attributable equity / 116.7m shares = JPY2,671/share book value vs JPY1,842 price).
key_risks_to_valuation: Honda Group concentration (~86-89% of revenue, ~22% of TS TECH's own voting rights held by Honda) means there is no realistic near-term diversification path if Honda's global volumes continue to shrink

China: Honda's China sales are down ~37.5% YTD through August 2026 and accelerating, with permanent ICE capacity closures through 2027; TS TECH's China segment already swung to an operating loss in Q1 FY2027

The 16th Medium-Term Plan (FY2027-29) asks investors to trust a numeric margin-recovery target from the same management that badly missed the equivalent 15th-plan target -- the base case discounts this explicitly rather than assuming credibility

A payout ratio above 100% of earnings (149% FY2026, ~134% guided FY2027) is being funded from the cash pile, not earnings; if the recovery plan slips again the dividend is the likely adjustment lever, removing a key support to the current price

Much of the recent reported earnings 'recovery' (Q1 FY2027 net income +172% YoY) is yen-weakness translation, not operational improvement, and would reverse if USD/JPY strengthens back toward its year-ago level
Material and growing non-controlling interests (~24-29% of consolidated net income) mean a rising share of any consolidated recovery does not flow through to TS TECH's own shareholders

inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY flows require a JPY-built WACC, not a USD default. House reference for JPY keiretsu industrials (used on 3116.T) is ~9%; applied here unchanged given comparable capital structure (net cash, no interest-bearing debt) and comparable Japan/US/China blended country-risk exposure. Cost of equity built from JGB 10yr ~1.5-2% + Japan equity risk premium ~6-7% plus a small small-cap/concentration premium; TS TECH carries materially higher customer-concentration risk than a diversified industrial (Honda ~86-89% of revenue), which is charged in the flows via probability weighting (see (f) below), not stacked again onto WACC.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial -- not adjusted. FY2025 lease liability repayments were JPY1.4-1.7bn/yr against JPY442-461bn revenue (<0.4%), described in the filing as 'mainly leases molds under finance lease contracts.' Lease liabilities (JPY4.7-5.8bn) sit inside 'Other financial liabilities' and are excluded from total_debt (which is interest-bearing borrowings, JPY0 both years). No lease principal is added back or deducted from the flows -- reported OCF/FCF is not meaningfully flattered by IFRS 16 here, unlike 3116.T (Toyota Boshoku) or MPG.NZ where lease payments were material.
inputs.nci_treatment: Material and growing: non-controlling interests (overseas subsidiaries, chiefly TS Tech Americas / TS Tech Detroit and Chinese JVs, not individually significant per Note 28) took 23.6% of consolidated net income in FY2025 (JPY2,672m of JPY11,303m total) and 26.1% in FY2026 (JPY2,524m of JPY9,658m total). Flows are modelled attributable-only: a combined tax+NCI leakage rate is charged inside cash_tax_rate_path, applied to EBIT (operating income only -- finance income is stripped separately per the interest-income rule, so EBIT here excludes finance income/costs and equity-method share). Combined leakage = 1-(1-statutory_tax)*(1-NCI_share_of_consolidated_NI). At FY2026 actuals (statutory 29.9%, NCI share 26.1%) that is ~48.2%; calibration check: attributable NOPAT implied (JPY10,325m x 0.518 = JPY5,349m) against reported attributable net income JPY7,134m is within non-operating noise (the JPY1.8bn gap is the FX-driven finance-income swing in Q1 FY2027 and the equity-method share, both excluded from this EBIT-based build by design). FY2025 calibration is tighter: implied JPY8,794m vs reported JPY8,630m, a 1.9% gap.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Owner-FCF DCF (component route) + owner-fcf-adaptations.md sections (a) currency, (c) minority interests, (d) excluded income/matching asset, (e) SBC-zero, (f) risk-charged-once. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials, consumer, keiretsu suppliers'. TS TECH is functionally the same situation as 3116.T (Toyota Boshoku, valued 14-Aug-2026 in this folder): a Japanese IFRS-reporting keiretsu automotive-seat Tier-1 supplier in a multi-year margin trough (operating margin 9.9% FY2018 peak -> 2.3% FY2026 trough) driven by customer (Honda) volume declines, China share loss to domestic EV makers, and cost inflation, with management guiding a specific numeric recovery path (16th Medium-Term Plan: 5.0% operating margin / 5.0% ROE by FY2029) that the PRIOR plan (15th MTP) badly missed (targeted 9.2% margin / 8.5% ROE for FY2026, delivered 2.3%/2.3%). A 10-year horizon is used because margins are still well below any plausible mature level in year 5 under every scenario. FIRST VALUATION of this ticker -- no prior DCF or memory entry exists; this build establishes the baseline.
inputs.recovery_plan_credibility_note: Base case ramps operating margin to 4.0% by year 5 and 4.5% by year 10 -- BELOW management's own 5.0%-by-FY2029 target -- specifically because the 15th Medium-Term Plan missed its analogous target by ~7 points (9.2% guided vs 2.3% delivered) and the China volume decline (Honda China sales -37.5% YTD through Aug-2026) that is driving the current trough shows no sign of stabilizing. The bull case gives management the benefit of the doubt and reaches close to the stated 5.0% target; the bear case assumes the recovery stalls at the FY2026 trough level plus only FX/cost-cutting tailwinds, consistent with a second missed medium-term plan.

bear.narrative: Bear case: the 16th Medium-Term Plan repeats the 15th's failure. Honda's China share loss (-37.5% YTD through Aug-2026, worse than the ~18% industry decline) does not stabilize and spreads pressure to Japan and Americas volumes as Honda's global production plans reset lower; the China segment (already operating-loss in Q1 FY2027) stays loss-making through the horizon. Non-Honda diversification wins (Maruti Suzuki, Changan Mazda) prove too small and too low-margin to offset the core Honda book's decline, so the JPY100bn FY2029 non-Honda target is missed as badly as the 15th plan's overall targets were. Operating margin stalls near the FY2026 trough (2.3-3%, implying ~4.8-5.5% EBITDA margin once D&A is added back) as cost programs are offset by continued wage inflation and a China restructuring drag; capex stays elevated for longer as growth investment (India, new plants) does not generate the expected volume. Combined tax+NCI leakage rises slightly (50%) as the higher-NCI overseas subsidiaries hold up better than the wholly-owned Japan business in relative terms. This is a real path, not a tail scenario, given the FY2026 result already undershot the (already-cut) 15th plan by this magnitude, which is why the bear weight is held above the house default.

base.narrative: Base case: FY2027 revenue follows management's own guidance (JPY440.0bn, -0.5% YoY) then grows modestly (1.5-2.0%/yr) as the non-Honda diversification push (Maruti Suzuki e VITARA, Changan Mazda EZ-60, India JV) offsets continued Honda-Japan/China volume attrition. Operating margin (EBITDA less the near-zero SBC and D&A) recovers from the FY2026 trough (2.3%) toward 4.0% by year 5 and 4.5% by year 10 -- roughly halfway to management's stated 5.0%-by-FY2029 target, reflecting genuine cost actions (Saitama plant consolidation into Gyoda, ~40% TS Americas HQ headcount cut, India/China lower-cost capacity) but discounting full achievement given the 15th Medium-Term Plan missed an even larger margin-recovery target by ~7 points. Capex stays elevated near-term per FY2027 guidance (JPY24.5bn, 5.6% of guided revenue) funding the India/Suzuki/Changan Mazda commercial-rights wins, then normalizes toward the historical ~3.3-4% range. Combined tax+NCI leakage starts at FY2026's calibrated ~48% and drifts down slightly as the (lower-NCI-share) Japan/non-Honda mix grows. Working capital is a modest cash drag on growth (wc_capture -8%), consistent with a manufacturer whose receivables and inventory build with volume. Terminal growth 1.5% reflects a maturing, single-digit-margin auto-parts supplier in a structurally slow-growth (ICE-to-EV transition, Japan demographic) end market; terminal cap multiple capped at 12x owner FCF, well below the SaaS-appropriate 20x, given the cyclical, capital-intensive, thin-margin nature of the business and its own multi-decade trading history below 1x book (PBR).

bull.narrative: Bull case: 16th Medium-Term Plan largely succeeds where the 15th failed. The Honda-share push toward 70%+ by FY2029 lands, the non-Honda strategic-OEM book scales toward the JPY100bn FY2029 target (Suzuki Group/Maruti Suzuki, Changan Mazda, new North American/European wins), and China stabilizes rather than continuing its ~20-37% YoY decline as Honda's localized EV/PHEV response gains traction. Operating margin reaches close to management's own 5.0% target by year 5 (8.5% EBITDA margin here, consistent with a ~5% operating margin once D&A of ~2.9% is netted) and drifts toward high-single-digit EBITDA margin by year 10 -- still below the FY2018 peak (9.9% operating margin) given a structurally more competitive, EV-transitioning global seat market. Yen weakness (a real FY2027 tailwind: USD/JPY 159.6 vs 144.6 YoY in Q1 FY2027) persists, supporting reported margins on translated overseas earnings. WACC nudged down 0.5pp to reflect lower execution risk once the recovery plan is visibly on track.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised well above the house default (15%) to 30% because this is not a hypothetical downside: the immediately prior medium-term plan (15th MTP, ending FY2026) missed its own operating-margin target by 7 points (9.2% guided vs 2.3% delivered) on the same Honda-concentration and China-share-loss dynamics that are still actively worsening (Honda China sales -37.5% YTD through Aug-2026, accelerating not stabilizing, per the Analysis JSON bear case). A near-90%-of-revenue dependence on a single customer group with no realistic near-term diversification path is exactly the 'single-customer dependency' condition the method flags for an elevated bear weight. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously (Honda share gains AND non-Honda scale-up AND China stabilization AND continued yen weakness) rather than any one lever. Base gets the remaining 45%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
